answer: Deposits are visible in falcon, and beacon reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 28% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 181 aliases, and each one needs its own funded vault account. That bill is paid per identity, so 399 aliases cost 276 times the single-account price. A hotel that takes a key deposit for every guest: you can book a hundred rooms under a hundred names, but the deposit is charged a hundred times.
